title: Red Hat RHCSA EX200 Course Notes
author: Frazier A. Smith, Ed.D.

exam.name: RHCSA
exam.coverLine: Shell skills, software, storage, services, networking, users, and SELinux on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, one exam objective at a time.
exam.trademarks: Red Hat, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, RHEL, and RHCSA are trademarks or registered trademarks of Red Hat, Inc. AlmaLinux is a trademark of the AlmaLinux OS Foundation.
exam.objectivesNote: The objective groups and wording referenced throughout follow the published Red Hat EX200 exam objectives for RHEL 10. Red Hat does not number the objectives; the group and topic numbers in these notes are the author's, added for cross-reference. Check the official objectives page before your exam; it is the final word on what the exam covers.
exam.introText: EX200 is a hands-on exam: you get live systems and a list of tasks, and the grader checks the end state of those systems, including after a reboot. There are no multiple-choice questions. These notes follow Red Hat's ten objective groups in order, and every topic carries a group and topic number so you can line it up against the official objectives, your course modules, and your lab work.
exam.tryLine: Do them on a RHEL 10, AlmaLinux 10, or Rocky Linux 10 lab machine. The exam grades what you can configure from memory under a clock, and reading about a command is not the same as running it.

objectives.title: Access a shell prompt and issue commands with correct syntax; create and edit text files
Use input-output redirection (>, >>, |, 2>, etc.)
Use grep and regular expressions to analyze text
Access remote systems using SSH; log in and switch users in multi-user targets
Archive, compress, unpack, and uncompress files using tar, gzip, and bzip2
Create, delete, copy, and move files and directories; create hard and soft links
List, set, and change standard ugo/rwx permissions
Locate, read, and use system documentation including man, info, and files in /usr/share/doc
Configure access to RPM repositories; install and remove RPM software packages
Configure access to Flatpak repositories; install and remove Flatpak software packages
Process script inputs ($1, $2, etc.); process output of shell commands within a script
Conditionally execute code (use of: if, test, [], etc.)
Use looping constructs (for, etc.) to process file and command line input
Boot, reboot, and shut down a system normally; boot systems into different targets manually; interrupt the boot process in order to gain access to a system
Identify CPU/memory intensive processes and kill processes; adjust process scheduling; manage tuning profiles
Locate and interpret system log files and journals; preserve system journals
Start, stop, and check the status of network services; securely transfer files between systems
List, create, and delete partitions on GPT disks
Create and remove physical volumes; assign physical volumes to volume groups; create and delete logical volumes
Configure systems to mount file systems at boot by UUID or label; add new partitions, logical volumes, and swap to a system non-destructively
Create, mount, unmount, and use VFAT, ext4, and XFS file systems
Mount and unmount network file systems using NFS; configure autofs
Extend existing logical volumes
Diagnose and correct file permission problems
Schedule tasks using at, cron, and systemd timer units
Start and stop services and configure services to start automatically at boot; configure systems to boot into a specific target automatically
Configure time service clients
Install and update software packages from Red Hat Content Delivery Network, a remote repository, or from the local file system
Modify the system bootloader
Configure IPv4 and IPv6 addresses; configure network services to start automatically at boot
Configure hostname resolution
Restrict network access using firewalld and firewall-cmd
Create, delete, and modify local user accounts; change passwords and adjust password aging for local user accounts
Create, delete, and modify local groups and group memberships
Configure privileged access
Configure firewall settings using firewall-cmd/firewalld
Manage default file permissions
Configure key-based authentication for SSH
Set enforcing and permissive modes for SELinux; list and identify SELinux file and process context
Restore default file contexts; manage SELinux port labels; use Boolean settings to modify system SELinux settings
